quote: Marrowind would then have to seek reformation or rely on the APA's order-of-precedence clause (§ 10.12) to claw back assets it intentionally retained.
reason: Most of the criterion is met. The memo flags Bill of Sale § 1.1(b): its 'Purchased Assets' definition covers all assets 'used or held for use in the Business' with no Excluded Assets carve-out. It explains this would convey Seller's cash, the Albany facility and the HOLLIS trademark. It recommends adopting the Section 2.1 APA definition and expressly excluding the Excluded Assets. It fails on one required element: the point that, under APA § 10.12, the Bill of Sale controls as to its own subject matter. The memo reads § 10.12 the other way, as a clause Seller could use to recover the assets. Under § 10.12's carve-out, the conveyancing instrument would govern the conveyance, so the APA would not override it. The memo therefore understates the risk on the precise point the criterion requires.
